fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Detached Structure; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Water Feature; Landscaped Area; Perimeter Fencing; Equipment Storage Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Multiple Structures; Long Driveway; Water Feature; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a clearly visible address marker at the driveway entrance so responding units can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to help responders locate and align with the access point in low-light or smoky conditions.
• Post a property map or structure diagram near the driveway entrance showing the location of all structures, the water feature, and the equipment storage area.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and overhanging branches for its full length to allow emergency vehicles to reach all structures without obstruction.
• Identify and mark a dedicated turnaround area near the structures so emergency vehicles are not forced to back out the full length of the driveway.
• Establish a secondary foot access path to the rear of the property so responders are not solely dependent on the main driveway to reach all structures.
• Mark the water feature with visible boundary indicators so responders moving across the open terrain at night or in reduced visibility do not approach the edge unexpectedly.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and both detached structures so responders can move between buildings without navigating around parked equipment or landscaping.
• Keep the equipment storage area organized so responders can quickly identify and avoid stored hazards during operations.
• If the perimeter fencing includes a rear or side gate, keep it unlocked

wildfire.conditions: Open Green Space; Grass Cover; Open Terrain; Scattered Shrubs; Vegetation Near Structure; Water Feature; Small Structure; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Limited Turnaround Area; Multiple Access Routes
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly next to the small structure.
• Keep grass around the structure cut short, especially during dry months.
• Clear any dead or dry grass that accumulates near the base of the small structure.
• Remove any shrubs or grass that have grown close enough to touch the structure.
• Keep the area between scattered shrubs and the structure open and clear of plant material.
• Mark or clear a turnaround area near the structure to allow emergency vehicles to reposition without backing long distances.
• Keep all access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching shrubs.
• Maintain open ground between the water feature shoreline vegetation and the structure.
